newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary gives go-ahead for building societies.
newsitem.headline: Hungary gives go-ahead for building societies.

text.p: Hungary's government gave its final approval for the creation of building societies, government spokesman Elemer Kiss said on Thursday.
"The decree contains general rules for the functioning of the building societies," he told a news conference after the government meeting.
He added that building societies would be allowed to charge a maximum one percent for opening an account and a maximum one percent handling fee.
The bill allowing building societies to operate in Hungary came to effect on January 1 and banks and insurance companies were awaiting the government decree to give the final go-ahead.

The law specifies that a building society must have a minimum one billion forints ($5.6 million) in equity to begin operations. Interest rate on deposits will be three percent, while the deposits would be complemented with a 30 percent, or a maximum 36,000 forints, state subsidy per account per year.
Hungary has opted for the German 'Bausparkasse'-model in which building societies are separated from other types of financial institutions.
Earlier press reports said that at least three building societies are ready to go as the legal framework is completed.
One of them is Lakaskassza Rt, in which Austria's insurance group EA Generali controls 52 percent of the initial registered capital of one billion forints.

Both Hungary's Postabank Rt and the Hungarian banking arm of Austria's Creditanstalt-Bankverein have a 21 percent stake in Lakaskassza, while the Oesterreichische Volksbanken AG 's banking unit in Hungary holds six percent.
Hungary's largest commercial bank OTP, and Takarekbank Rt, which represents savings cooperatives is likely to enter the market in association with Germany's Bausparkasse Schwabish Hall.
